issues: No sign that the candidate gets around the measurement. It reads no files and makes no network calls. Test molecules are only featurized, and their labels are never used. The inner GroupKFold stacking groups the training fold by Murcko scaffold and uses training labels only.

No bug found that would make the result meaningless. KRR uses a Tanimoto kernel on the fingerprint matrix with the mean subtracted from the target. NNLS stacking without an intercept is fine for rank targets in [0, 1], and Spearman ignores scale anyway. If all NNLS weights come out zero, the code falls back to equal weights.

The change has a real side effect: the candidate drops the atompair and MACCS feature sets the incumbent averaged, and keeps Morgan only. That may explain part of the regression, from 0.5266 to 0.5438.

Recomputed z = (0.5438 - 0.5266) / (0.0070 * sqrt(2)) ≈ 1.74 worse for the candidate. This matches the harness's -1.729 apart from the sign convention and rounding of the noise sd. With one run on each side the evidence is weak, but rejecting is consistent with the numbers.
The candidate costs much more: 5 fits each of RF, KRR and LightGBM per outer fold, against 3 RF fits before. That is likely still within the 10-minute limit, but it is extra complexity for no gain.
